annotations.annotation: The pie chart represents different analytical layers in a study of content analysis, breaking them into categories(inner circle) and subcategories (outer circle). There are four main slices, each with further subcategories totaling 16 segments. The first segment is the "Perception Layer" shown in dark blue, comprising 40.4% of the chart and includes subcategories like "Environmental Perception & Reasoning", "Counting & Statistics", "Music Theory", "Correlation Analysis", "Temporal Analysis" and "Spatial Analysis". The second segment is the "Semantic Layer" in medium blue, representing 41.2%, with subcategories such as "Content Analysis", "Emotion & Intention", "Aesthetic Analysis" and "Speaker Analysis". The third segment, the "Cultural Layer", is also light grey and comprises 14.1%, with subcategories like "Culture of Speaker", "Imagination" and "Professional Knowl & Reasoning". The fourth segment, "Signal Layer", in the light purple, making up 4.3%, with subcategories like "Anomaly Detection", "Acoustic Quality Analysis and Audio Difference Analysis". The accompanying subcategories are labeled, and their arrangement visibly emphasizes the main analytical layers, though no segment appears to be offset or exploded. The chart includes percentage labels within the slices for the inner slices only and the segments are presented in no order, without a specific legend provided. The center part is white, then followed by the chart contents.
